review.summary: The commit fixes a crash in the bidiagonal SVD iteration (`__svd!` in src/svd.jl) where, after deflating a zero singular value and decrementing n2, the loop continued with stale submatrix bounds and could reduce over an empty range. The fix jumps back to the top of the loop (`@goto top`) to re-locate the active submatrix after deflation and defers the σ⁻/thresh estimation to inside the loop. Issue #121 documents the concrete user-visible failure (`rank(BigFloat[0 0; 1 -1])` throwing a MethodError about reducing over an empty collection), introduced by an earlier PR #108, and PR #122 closes it.
review.validation_risks: The commit also adds/reworks two `@debug` statements; these are non-behavioral under default logging but the un-minimized patch mixes diagnostics with the fix. The issue title in #122 uses the word 'Refactor', which could be mistaken for a non-bug change, but the underlying defect is a hard error. The fix relies on control flow (`@goto top`) and a label presumably already present at the loop head, so applying the minimized patch out of context could fail to compile if the label is missing. Bit-level singular value output may shift slightly for other inputs because thresh is now computed inside the loop, so exact-value assertions elsewhere could be sensitive; the reported passing full suite mitigates this.

swe.interface:
Function: svdvals(A::AbstractMatrix{T}) where T
Location: src/svd.jl (non‑bang wrapper that calls `svdvals!`)
Inputs: 
- `A`: an `AbstractMatrix` (e.g., `Matrix{BigFloat}`) containing numeric entries. No explicit keyword arguments are required; an optional `tol` keyword may be supplied to control the deflation tolerance.
Outputs: 
- Returns a `Vector{T}` containing the singular values of `A` in descending order. For matrices that are rank‑deficient or have zero‑size active sub‑matrices, the function now returns zeros for the missing singular values instead of throwing a `MethodError`.
Description: Computes the singular values of a matrix using the GenericLinearAlgebra SVD implementation. It safely handles edge cases where the active submatrix becomes empty after deflation (e.g., the `Issue 121` matrices) by returning a complete list of singular values without errors.

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports that a recent PR broke the deflation step in the SVD routine, causing rank and svdvals to error on certain BigFloat matrices. The added tests explicitly assert the correct singular values for these edge‑case matrices, matching the described expected behavior. The tests directly verify the functionality described in the issue without needing external knowledge or naming conventions, and no unrelated test coupling or ambiguities are present. Therefore the task is clearly specified and solvable (A).

swe.problem_statement:
Deflation breaks edge case
It seems https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/GenericLinearAlgebra.jl/pull/108 broke some edge cases.
Consider for instance:
```julia
julia> rank(BigFloat[0 0; 1 -1])
ERROR: MethodError: reducing over an empty collection is not allowed; consider supplying `init` to the reducer
Stacktrace:
  [1] mapreduce_empty(#unused#::typeof(identity), op::Function, T::Type)
    @ Base ./reduce.jl:367
  [2] reduce_empty(op::Base.MappingRF{typeof(identity), typeof(max)}, #unused#::Type{BigFloat})
    @ Base ./reduce.jl:356
  [3] reduce_empty_iter
    @ ./reduce.jl:379 [inlined]
  [4] mapreduce_empty_iter(f::Function, op::Function, itr::SubArray{BigFloat, 1, Vector{BigFloat}, Tuple{UnitRange{Int64}}, true}, ItrEltype::Base.HasEltype)
    @ Base ./reduce.jl:375
  [5] _mapreduce(f::typeof(identity), op::typeof(max), #unused#::IndexLinear, A::SubArray{BigFloat, 1, Vector{BigFloat}, Tuple{UnitRange{Int64}}, true})
    @ Base ./reduce.jl:427
  [6] _mapreduce_dim
    @ ./reducedim.jl:365 [inlined]
  [7] #mapreduce#765
    @ ./reducedim.jl:357 [inlined]
  [8] mapreduce
    @ ./reducedim.jl:357 [inlined]
  [9] #_maximum#783
    @ ./reducedim.jl:999 [inlined]
 [10] _maximum
    @ ./reducedim.jl:999 [inlined]
 [11] #_maximum#782
    @ ./reducedim.jl:998 [inlined]
 [12] _maximum
    @ ./reducedim.jl:998 [inlined]
 [13] #maximum#780
    @ ./reducedim.jl:994 [inlined]
 [14] maximum
    @ ./reducedim.jl:994 [inlined]
 [15] __svd!(B::Bidiagonal{BigFloat, Vector{BigFloat}}, U::Nothing, Vᴴ::Nothing; tol::BigFloat)
    @ GenericLinearAlgebra ~/.julia/dev/GenericLinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:224
 [16] _svdvals!(B::Bidiagonal{BigFloat, Vector{BigFloat}}; tol::BigFloat)
    @ GenericLinearAlgebra ~/.julia/dev/GenericLinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:252
 [17] #svdvals!#33
    @ ~/.julia/dev/GenericLinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:539 [inlined]
 [18] svdvals!(A::Matrix{BigFloat}; tol::BigFloat)
    @ GenericLinearAlgebra ~/.julia/dev/GenericLinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:567
 [19] svdvals!
    @ ~/.julia/dev/GenericLinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:564 [inlined]
 [20] svdvals
    @ ~/.julia/juliaup/julia-1.8.5+0.x64.linux.gnu/share/julia/stdlib/v1.8/LinearAlgebra/src/svd.jl:243 [inlined]
 [21] rank(A::Matrix{BigFloat}; atol::Float64, rtol::BigFloat)
    @ LinearAlgebra ~/.julia/juliaup/julia-1.8.5+0.x64.linux.gnu/share/julia/stdlib/v1.8/LinearAlgebra/src/generic.jl:977
 [22] rank(A::Matrix{BigFloat})
    @ LinearAlgebra ~/.julia/juliaup/julia-1.8.5+0.x64.linux.gnu/share/julia/stdlib/v1.8/LinearAlgebra/src/generic.jl:975
 [23] top-level scope
    @ REPL[13]:1
```
In the code `n1 = 1` and `n2 = 2` then because `d = [-1, 0]`, `n2` is decreased to 1 by
https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/GenericLinearAlgebra.jl/blob/8414b44b7ac3325c5e2233728e6b1cf64a416ecf/src/svd.jl#L212
After that
https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/GenericLinearAlgebra.jl/blob/8414b44b7ac3325c5e2233728e6b1cf64a416ecf/src/svd.jl#L224
fails because the interval `n1:n2-1` is now empty and
https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/GenericLinearAlgebra.jl/blob/8414b44b7ac3325c5e2233728e6b1cf64a416ecf/src/svd.jl#L233
fails because `n2 - 1` is now `0`.
